paper_title: AI-guided patient stratification improves outcomes and efficiency in the AMARANTH Alzheimer's Disease clinical trial
prediction_task: AD patient stratification for clinical trial enrichment (trained on ADNI, applied to AMARANTH trial)

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Results are not very impressive — mainly the difference between sensitivity and specificity. Existing approaches show much better performance up to 97% accuracy. Technical contributions are limited.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Clarified that the novelty is cross-dataset generalization (ADNI→AMARANTH without retraining), not raw accuracy. Added context for existing methods.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: The most critical element — that the model was trained on ADNI and applied to AMARANTH without retraining — is not sufficiently emphasised. This represents the key contribution and should be made clear earlier.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Restructured introduction and abstract to emphasize cross-dataset generalization upfront.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Since the true treatment effect in clinical trials is inherently unknown, further discussion of what evidence supports the model's consistency across datasets would strengthen the manuscript.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Added discussion of external consistency evidence and limitations of post-hoc trial analysis.

reviewer_concerns.concern_text: Figures need axes labels and units. The outcomes and methodology are not reflecting the claim of interpretable AI model.
reviewer_concerns.author_response: Improved all figure labels and added interpretability analysis section.

reviewer_strengths.text: Highly significant and original contribution. Demonstrates that ML model trained on ADNI can be applied to AMARANTH trial without retraining — going well beyond reliable insights: rescuing a clinical trial. Provides generalisable framework for precision medicine.
